notes.1: Some candidates did not read this question carefully enough. The question required candidates to identify the instruments necessary to measure the volume of an irregularly shaped rock – it did not require the mass of the rock as well.
notes.3: This question proved challenging for many candidates. Stronger candidates realised that they needed to find the total time taken (100 s up the hill plus 50 s down) and divide this into the total distance travelled (600 m).
notes.5: Although the question was answered reasonably well, there were a significant number of candidates who thought that there must be a resultant force in the direction of the velocity in order to keep an object moving at constant speed in that direction.
notes.6: Only stronger candidates answered this question correctly. Many candidates thought that response A was correct as they applied the formula for density without thinking the problem through.
notes.8: Although many candidates were able to solve this problem, a large minority gave C as their answer, suggesting that they had difficulty with the manipulation of equations.
notes.10: Although most candidates showed a good grasp of energy transfers, some candidates thought that the ball started with kinetic energy and this was transferred to gravitational potential energy.
notes.12: This question proved challenging for many candidates. Although most candidates ruled out option A, (chemical change) all other options were selected by equal numbers of candidates.
notes.13: Almost all candidates recognised that the lower points are at higher pressures than the upper points. However a number of candidates thought that the less dense liquid would produce a greater pressure than the more dense liquid.
notes.14: Stronger candidates showed an understanding of the theory of the use of a manometer, and also the ability to think through a problem in a logical fashion.
notes.16: This question proved challenging for most candidates. The simple concept of mass was not well understood.
notes.18: Many candidates did not link the period of time that the temperature is constant, in a cooling experiment, with the solidification of the liquid. Either that or they failed to understand that a liquid melts at the same temperature that it solidifies.
notes.19: The question was answered well by candidates who had experience of doing the experiment but it was more challenging for candidates has only seen it described in a book.
notes.20: Only stronger candidates were able to answer this question correctly. The logic is that the rise in temperature of the cooler plate will be slowest when there is least energy emitted from the hotter plate (shiny white) and when it absorbs the smallest proportion of that energy (once more, the shiny white plate).
notes.28: The vast majority of candidates recognised that the charge carriers in a metal are free electrons but there was some confusion as to their direction of flow.
notes.31: Some candidates incorrectly believed that the current in a circuit increases when the resistance of a variable resistance is increased.
notes.32: Understanding that a parallel circuit has less resistance than a series circuit (and therefore more current) was not well understood. Candidates chose each of the four options in almost equal numbers.
notes.33: A number of candidates showed a lack of understanding of parallel circuits but stronger candidates were about to answer correctly.
notes.38: Only stronger candidates recognised the correct diagram with many thinking that the superscript referred to the number of neutrons in the nucleus rather than the number of nucleons.
notes.39: Many candidates lacked an understanding of background radiation and some thought it was due to the rock itself while other candidates thought that it is infra-red radiation from the Sun.
notes.40: This question proved challenging to many candidates. The most common error was to simply find the half-life of the isotope and not to go on to use that to find the remaining mass of the isotope.
notes.key_messages: Candidates should be reminded to read the questions carefully to ensure they understand what is being asked.
notes.general_comments: Candidates found Questions 2, 9, 11, 13, 25, 26, 30, 36 and 37 accessible. However, Questions 3, 6, 12, 20, 22, 32, 35 and 39 proved very challenging for many candidates.
